title: PRD: Minimal Determinism Contract & Launch Litmus for Hosted Generation/Embeddings/Rerank
creator: Ava Patel
description: This PRD defines a minimal, enforceable determinism contract for the hosted inference surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). The goal is to narrow scope to a small, testable set of behavioral guarantees that developers can depend on during canary and GA. The document includes clarified requirements, a scope-freeze proposal, acceptance criteria, and a launch litmus and cutover checklist that ties together evals, telemetry, and rollback gates.
background: Customers building production features rely on predictable quality and repeatable behavior across incremental runtime and model changes. Full determinism is infeasible across all models/hardware; this PRD proposes a minimal contract (seeded randomness bounds, stable embedding vectors for identical inputs within quality tolerance, and deterministic rerank ordering for identical inputs) plus pragmatic controls (eval gates, rollout slices) to avoid regressions at launch.
scope: In scope: hosted endpoints for text generation (chat/completions), embeddings, and reranking. Acceptance criteria, test harness definitions, canary rollout plan, telemetry dashboards, and rollback playbooks. Out-of-scope: provider-level kernel selection internals, deep model architecture changes, private/VPC deployments (addressed in separate P0).
out_of_scope: Hardware-level determinism guarantees, full reproducibility across quantization modes, SDK surface changes unrelated to contract, enterprise-only private deployments.
requirements_clarification: 1) Determinism metric: define a suite of deterministic probes (token sequence identity for seeded calls with fixed random seed, embedding cosine similarity thresholds for identical inputs, and rerank order stability for identical feature inputs). 2) Behavioral scope per endpoint: chat/completions — seeded generation repeatability within token divergence window; embeddings — vector similarity > 0.995 for identical inputs across the same model version and quantization profile; rerank — stable pairwise ordering for identical input batches. 3) Tolerance windows and allowed variance defined per model family. 4) API contract: add optional 'seed' parameter documented as experimental; callers without seed get best-effort stability but no deterministic guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: Determinism Litmus: for 1000 randomized canonical prompts with seed parameter set, generated token sequences must match exactly for 99.9% of cases across two independent hosts running the runtime. Failure cases logged and limited to known nondeterministic operators.

Embeddings Consistency: for 500 canonical texts, cosine similarity must be >= 0.995 between two runs of the same model version and quantization profile; any drift above threshold must be triaged within 48 hours and blocked from GA if systemic.

Rerank Stability: for 200 canonical query-document batches, ordering must be identical in 99% of cases when input features and model version match; documented nondeterministic ties allowed with stable tie-break policy.
API Contract: 'seed' parameter present in spec, documented, SDKs expose it, and behavior is included in API changelog and migration guide.
E2E Smoke Tests: CI must include generation, embedding, and rerank deterministic smoke runs as part of the canary pipeline; failures send alerts and block promotion.
Telemetry: launch dashboards display per-model determinism violation rates, token-level variance, and customer-impacting incidents; SLO for determinism violations set to <= 0.1% in GA tier.
Rollback Gate: an automated rollback trigger exists when determinism violation rate exceeds 0.5% for 15 minutes on canary or exceeds 0.2% on GA across > 5% of tenant traffic.
Documentation: public API docs, migration notes, and a short FAQ must be published before cutover.
Security: no sensitive customer data is added to deterministic probes; probes are synthetic or anonymized.
Sign-offs: PM, Eng (runtime lead), SRE, Docs, and Legal (if export controls apply) must sign off in the PRD comment thread before GA rollout.
success_metrics: Primary: percent of seeded-generation exact match (target >= 99.9%). Secondary: embedding drift rate (<0.5% weekly), rerank ordering violations (<1% per week), number of customer incidents caused by nondeterminism (target 0 for first 90 days).
risks: Model upstream changes (weights/ops) introduce nondeterminism beyond our control
Quantized execution paths on some hardware show higher variance
Customers rely on undocumented behavior; clarifying the contract may require migration support
Telemetry blind spots if probes aren't representative of real traffic
test_plan: Unit: deterministic operator-level tests in runtime repo covering RNG, attention kernels, and KV cache reinstatement
Integration: cross-host seeded generation runs with CI harness comparing token streams and hashing outputs
Embedding regression: nightly vector drift job over canonical corpus and alerting on threshold breaches
Rerank stability: pairwise ordering comparison harness for synthetic batches and seeded tie-breaker tests
Load: run deterministic probes under typical QPS to ensure stability under load and during autoscale events
Canary: run full suite against 1% traffic slice for 48 hours prior to ramp
rollout_checklist: Scope freeze: lock model versions and quantization profiles for canary stage
Infra: ensure canary hosts run runtime-1.20 with deterministic-kernel flag enabled
CI: deterministic smoke tests green in main and canary branches
Docs: API spec updated with 'seed' parameter, examples, and migration notes
Dashboards: determinism panel added to console runtime metrics with alert rules
Canary: 1% traffic for 48h, observe litmus metrics; if pass, increase to 10% for 24h
Stakeholder checks: PM, SRE, Docs, Solutions Eng sign off after canary
GA: increment traffic in staged ramp with ongoing monitoring; ensure rollback playbook is ready
Post-GA monitoring: 30-day focused watch with daily summary and on-call rotation for determinism incidents
rollback_playbook: Automated: route traffic away from canary hosts to baseline pool if violation threshold breached
Manual: immediate deploy rollback to previous runtime image tagged stable-1.19 if automated routing insufficient
Communication: notify customers via status page and targeted email for affected tenants when customer-impacting nondeterminism is detected
Postmortem: on-call writes a 72-hour incident report for any rollback triggered by determinism violations
decision_log: 2026-02-15: Chose minimal contract approach over exhaustive determinism due to engineering cost and model variance
2026-02-20: Agreed to add optional 'seed' parameter rather than enforce seed for all calls to avoid changing client behavior
2026-03-02: Set acceptance thresholds (99.9% generation match, 0.995 embedding cosine) after pilot runs
2026-03-08: Decided on canary slice progression: 1% -> 10% -> staged ramp, with automated rollback rules
